opportunities.title: The Market Didn't Blink: $1B Flowed Into Bitcoin ETFs the Same Week Coldcard Got Drained
opportunities.why_now: ETFs just posted their best inflow week since April in the immediate aftermath of a $247M hardware wallet exploit, and even Bloomberg can't tie them together — that disconnect is the whole thesis of this channel.
opportunities.angle: Markets-meets-security op-ed: security incidents no longer move price, institutional flows have priced out retail panic — with the Coldcard timeline as Exhibit A.

opportunities.title: Self-Custody Just Had Its Worst Month: Coldcard + BTCPay Prove 'Not Your Keys' Isn't Enough
opportunities.why_now: Coldcard's exploit made July the second-worst month of 2026 for losses, and days later BTCPay's Lightning nodes got actively drained too — two pillars of the sovereignty stack failed in the same week.
opportunities.angle: Incident post-mortem tying both hacks together: hardware wallets and self-hosted payment infra both got popped, so what's actually left of the 'not your keys, not your coins' promise.

opportunities.title: Coldcard Hackers Just Told You How Confident They Are: 64 BTC and 200 ETH Straight Into Mixers
opportunities.why_now: The attackers moved the stolen funds to mixers within days of the exploit going public, giving a live case study in post-hack laundering speed and on-chain forensics.
opportunities.angle: On-chain trace breakdown: what the mixer routing reveals about attacker sophistication and whether Chainalysis-style tracing (see their Bybit/Penlink work) can still catch it.

opportunities.title: Crypto's Physical Security Problem Just Got a Price Tag: $30M in Wrench Attacks, France Now a Hotspot
opportunities.why_now: Chainalysis just quantified violent crypto attacks in 2026 at $30M with France emerging as a new hotspot, turning a scary anecdote trend into hard data.
opportunities.angle: Opsec explainer: self-custody's real threat model isn't just malware, it's a wrench and your address history — practical steps to reduce visible wealth signals.

opportunities.title: AI Is Now Finding Bitcoin's Bugs Before Humans Do — That's Not Entirely Good News
opportunities.why_now: A Bitcoin red team just went on record saying AI tooling is surfacing critical exploits across core projects, right as Coldcard and BTCPay incidents show attackers are already ahead.
opportunities.angle: Dual-use tooling analysis: if AI is finding these bugs for defenders, it's finding them for attackers too — what that means for the pace of infrastructure hacks going forward.
